answer: Require every agent to anchor its identity to a scarce, non-transferable credential: a hardware-backed cipher key bound to a verified computation history. New identities start with zero reputation and must complete costly, rate-limited useful work before earning transaction rights, so spawning thousands of fake agents costs real compute and time rather than just new addresses. Unlike a fable where one actor wears many masks for free, this makes each additional identity progressively expensive, while honest agents keep their accumulated anchor intact across sessions.
